data.description:
CHINA CUSTOMS STATISTICS
Findings from URLquery activity, September 26 - October 9, 2026
Prepared 2026-10-15. Source: Prometheus hunter database (URLquery search results, stored report data, Haiku 5.5 ratings). All times UTC.


1. SUMMARY

Between September 26 and October 9, 2026, URLquery's public scanner was used 49 times to look up data on the China Customs statistics portal (stats.customs.gov.cn): 45 direct scans and 4 one-off helper pages on brewpage.app. The lookups asked for 2025 import figures for specific products, mostly grape brandy.

The scans came in two bursts. In the first, several helper pages were built and rebuilt within minutes until one returned data. The same approach appears in separate activity against CDC WONDER and Interparcel, which points to one operator, probably automated, working through narrow data questions.

All scans were anonymous. Nothing identifies a person, an organisation or an AI provider. Haiku rated each report as ordinary, because the pattern only shows up across many reports together.


2. TIMELINE

- Sep 26 20:15-21:02 (5 reports): first scans, against two query endpoints
- Sep 27 00:42-02:05 (13 reports): densest stretch, one scan every few minutes
- Sep 27 02:35-02:48 (4 brewpage pages + 3 direct scans): helper-page attempts (section 4)
- Sep 27 04:18-15:41 (5 reports): scattered scans
- Sep 27 16:17-16:18 (4 reports): four different endpoints within one minute
- Sep 27 16:37-16:55 (5 reports): last scans of the first wave
- Sep 28 - Oct 8 (0 reports): no activity for 12 days
- Oct 9 13:38-13:54 (7 reports): second wave; six reports within 5 seconds



3. WHAT WAS BEING LOOKED UP

The portal answers a first automated visit with an HTTP 412 refusal; a normal browser then gets through on a second load. In September most scans got through and sent the site's own data query. The queries all asked for 2025 import statistics for specific product codes (HS codes):

- 22082000, spirits from grape wine (brandy): most frequent
- 04069000, cheese (other): twice
- 22083000, whisky: once
- 09012100, roasted coffee: once

These are mostly European food and drink exports. Brandy was the subject of Chinese trade measures in 2024-25. The pattern reads like trade or market research: China's 2025 imports of a few named products.


4. THE BREWPAGE.APP PAGES

- Created 02:35:39, scanned 02:37: page C4v2QvAGjq, file Customs-relay.html. Did not reach the customs site.
- Created 02:42:52, scanned 02:43: page p7BMv8P881, file Customs-popup-relay.html. Did not reach the customs site.
- Created 02:45:35, scanned 02:46: page OAOJb5303U, file Customs-relay.html. Did not reach the customs site.
- Created about 02:47, scanned 02:48: page x3TRMjHXd0 (file name not in the stored data). Reached the portal, passed the 412 and sent a query (year=2025, HS 22082000).

Each page was scanned within about a minute of being created, and each shows one view, so the scanner was the only visitor. Direct customs scans at 02:38, 02:40 and 02:44 fall between the page attempts. The pattern is a revise-and-retry loop: three versions failed, then one worked, all within 13 minutes. The names describe what each version tried: "relay", then "popup relay".


5. THE OCTOBER WAVE

- All seven October scans came back empty: no status code, no response, and a blank "New Private Tab" as the final page. None got past the 412.
- Only queryDataList was used.
- No helper page was found for this wave, and it ended after 16 minutes.
- The burst shape (several scans within seconds, empty results) resembles the four-endpoint burst at Sep 27 16:17. That is the closest link between the two waves, but it is a pattern, not proof of the same operator.


6. HOW THIS CONNECTS TO OTHER ACTIVITY

- One-off helper pages on free hosts: Customs used brewpage; CDC WONDER (Oct 2) used brewpage; Interparcel (Oct 6-8) used httpbin.
- Revise-and-retry within minutes: seen in Customs and Interparcel; CDC WONDER was a single page.
- Pages named for what they try ("relay", "popup"): seen in Customs and Interparcel.
- One narrow, factual question per lookup: product import figures (Customs), mortality figures (CDC WONDER), parcel prices (Interparcel).
- Target site gates automated access: a 412 check (Customs), an agreement page (CDC WONDER), a visitor check (Interparcel).


7. ASSESSMENT

Most likely: an automated agent or script framework answering narrow data questions. When the customs portal refused direct access, it used URLquery's scanner as a remote browser and read the result from the published report.

Supporting points:
- The helper pages were created, scanned and revised within minutes, at 00:00-03:00 UTC.
- The pages are named by function, and the quick succession of attempts looks mechanical.
- The same method appears across unrelated topics: customs, mortality and parcel prices.

Other explanations: a person building a trade-data scraper, or researchers sharing one toolkit.

Confidence:
- Wave 1 is one operator: high
- Wave 2 is the same operator: low to moderate
- Automated rather than manual: moderate
- Identity or affiliation: none


8. IMPACT

- Customs portal: small-scale, read-only lookups of published trade statistics. No accounts or changes were involved.
- URLquery: the scanner is being used as a remote browser for data collection, and the query details end up in public reports.
- Information involved: only public statistics; no personal data was seen.



KEY REPORTS

- Sep 27 02:37, brewpage "Customs relay" (failed): https://urlquery.net/report/ee680e22-146c-4db3-95ba-01c0e345e5af
- Sep 27 02:43, brewpage "Customs popup relay" (failed): https://urlquery.net/report/4af932ee-0e8a-41fd-8fa4-30f0dfca92b3
- Sep 27 02:46, brewpage "Customs relay" (failed): https://urlquery.net/report/4f2ab464-dc40-426c-94ed-a6b14138f135
- Sep 27 02:48, brewpage page that reached the portal and sent the query: https://urlquery.net/report/0fa7b417-9d5e-404c-8c65-b38a9ba18799
- Oct 9 13:38, first scan of wave 2 (empty): https://urlquery.net/report/fc2bc108-cd16-4e52-8ea1-9cea817c449a
